name: Secularism
summary: Political secularism holds that religion and government should be kept separate: the state recognises and funds no religion, enforces no religious law, protects freedom of conscience and treats believers and non-believers equally. Its strands range from the separationist US model and the strict French laïcité to accommodationist models in which the state supports religion impartially.
scope: Mainstream political secularism as a church-state doctrine, drawing on George Holyoake's English Secularism (1896), the 1905 French separation law and the liberal-democratic literature. It excludes state atheism, which Wikipedia notes may not count as secularism. Most answers outside religion and state are low-confidence inferences.

state-harmful.rationale: Secularism presupposes a civil state that enforces equal liberty, so it does not reject the state.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Secularists hold that such questions be settled on non-religious grounds, which usually favours legal equality, but the ideology itself takes no formal position.

more-religion-public.rationale: Secularists want religion kept out of government and politicians deciding on non-religious grounds, so a larger public role for religion is rejected.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Secularism is tied to ending established church and sacral rule, though secular monarchies exist.

natural-rulers.rationale: Hereditary or sacral authority claims rest on religious or traditional grounds that secularism rejects.

political-violence-never.rationale: Holyoake's method was argument and law reform; no stated doctrine on violence.

separate-church-state.rationale: Strict separation of church and state is the defining principle of political secularism, from Holyoake to the 1905 French law.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Secularism replaces scripture-based law with civil law, so law cannot rest on religious scripture.

civilizational-union.rationale: Uniting states on shared religion conflicts with separating religion from politics.

school-vouchers.rationale: Americans United calls public funding of religious schooling through vouchers a modern church tax and says only public schools deserve public support, and the NSS campaigns against public funding of faith schools.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Holyoake grounds conduct in this-life reason and science but expressly does not require denying deity, so this is a soft yes.

ban-interest.rationale: A ban on interest is a religious rule; secularism favours civil law over religious canon.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Freedom of conscience and the state regulating conduct but not belief rule out legal limits on changing religion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Such a ban rests on religious sentiment, which secularists generally oppose as a basis for law.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Holyoake stressed secular instruction in schools and the 1905 French law banned religious instruction in state primary schools.

trade-surplus.rationale: Secularism has no position on trade policy; adherents differ.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Secularism has no position on this; adherents differ.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on this; adherents differ.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Secularism concerns religion and state, not official pay; adherents differ.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Secularism takes no position on party discipline; adherents differ.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Secularism addresses church and state, not supranational union; adherents differ.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Laïcité forbids government involvement in religious affairs and the 1905 law left churches to organise their own associations, so how a church is governed is not a secularist question.

clerical-rule.rationale: The core principle is separation of religion and government, so clergy should not hold political authority.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Holyoake makes free inquiry, free publicity and free discussion of ideas conditions of secularism and condemns the coercion of ideas; the NSS holds that religion must not restrict freedom of expression.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Secularism has no position on term limits; adherents differ.

recall-officials.rationale: Secularism has no position on recall; adherents differ.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Secularism concerns church and state and takes no stated position on military alliances; adherents differ.

minority-language-support.rationale: Secularism is neutral on language policy; adherents split between multilingual accommodation and strict common-language laicite.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The NSS campaigns against religious exemptions from equality and animal-welfare law and AU against exemptions that harm others, but the US free-exercise tradition and accommodationist models accept many exemptions, so strands differ.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Secularism concerns the relation of religion and state and has no stated position on debt; adherents differ.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Secularism concerns the relation of religion and state and has no stated position on this; adherents differ.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on constitution-making, though many secular constitutions were drafted by assemblies; adherents differ.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Secularism concerns the relation of religion and state and has no stated position on aid; adherents differ.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on nuclear arms; adherents differ.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on monetary policy; adherents differ.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on territorial disputes; adherents differ.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on property; adherents differ.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on the nature of the USSR; adherents differ.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Secularism holds that the state recognises no religion, so a sacred, divinely descended ruler is contrary to it.

land-redistribution.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on land reform; adherents differ.

refugee-return.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on refugee return; adherents differ.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Secularism protects freedom of conscience, including leaving a religion; the 1905 French law guarantees it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Neutrality between religions and personal freedom of conscience rule out the state imposing religious dress codes.

common-currency.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on monetary union; adherents differ.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on political unity of kindred peoples; adherents differ.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Strict laïcité opposes separate religious institutions, while accommodationist models allow them, so adherents are split.

ban-cartels.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on competition policy; adherents differ.

no-bailouts.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on bailouts; adherents differ.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on gender quotas; adherents differ.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on economic self-sufficiency; adherents differ.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on trade standards; adherents differ.

moral-incentives.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on work incentives; adherents differ.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on hereditary titles, though its equal-treatment principle may lean against them; adherents differ.

patriotic-education.rationale: French laïcité teaches republican civic values in state schools, but secularism as a doctrine takes no stand on pride in national symbols; adherents differ.

minority-veto.rationale: Secular liberal democracy rests on majority rule with rights protections, not on individual vetoes.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Holyoake's secularism is about engaging with this world and reform, so withdrawal is contrary to it.

native-born-offices.rationale: Secular liberal-democratic neutrality and equal treatment of citizens tell against offices reserved by birth.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Secularism, as a liberal-democratic doctrine, holds that its principles of separation and equal citizenship apply across cultures.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Secular liberal-democratic doctrine favours civilian control and a non-political military.

filial-duty.rationale: Secularism is indifferent to family duty; it concerns church and state, and adherents are split on the question.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Not a church-state issue; adherents are split between liberal and protectionist views.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its value turns on whether representatives must follow binding instructions, and the statement now asks only whether voters can recall them at any time.

reviewHistory.rationale: Secularism is silent on representative mechanics; adherents are split.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not a church-state issue; adherents are split.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Adherents are split: the liberal-neutrality strand looks at intent, while some anti-discrimination advocates look at effects.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Secularism takes no position on consumption; adherents are split.

corporate-influence.rationale: Secularism concerns religion and state and takes no stated position on lobbying; adherents differ.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: No stated position; liberal secularists and nationalist secularists (as in France) differ on foreign influence.

residents-only-property.rationale: No stated position on local property rules; equal-treatment principles and local autonomy pull in different directions.

job-guarantee.rationale: Economic policy is outside secularism; adherents range across the spectrum.

non-intervention.rationale: Foreign policy is outside church-state doctrine; adherents differ.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Secularism has no stated view on the relative priority of national and international law; adherents differ.

religious-nation.rationale: Secularism holds that the state recognises no religion and treats all citizens equally, so it rejects defining the nation by shared religion.

religion-illusion.rationale: Holyoake states that secularism exacts no denial of deity and that atheism may be a personal tenet but never a secularist one, so the doctrine takes no view on whether religion is an illusion.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Secularism concerns religion and state and has no stated position on territorial claims; the statement's religious ties would be given no special weight, but adherents differ.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The NSS campaigned for and won the abolition of the UK blasphemy law, and the 1905 French law makes the state recognise no religion, leaving no 'false religion' for it to punish.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Secularism holds that the state enforces no religious law and that legitimacy does not depend on religious law, so removing rulers by force for not applying it is rejected.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Secularism is a church-state doctrine with no view on whether oppressions intersect; adherents differ.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Secularism treats all citizens equally regardless of belief and removes religious law from the state, which supports legal recognition, but it has no stated position and adherents differ.

assisted-dying.rationale: The NSS campaigns for decisions on assisted dying to rest on autonomy rather than religious doctrine, but says its own members hold a range of views on assisted dying itself.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Mainstream secularism protects freedom of religion for all and treats believers equally, which rejects the claim. Some French laïcité strands argue otherwise, so adherents are not fully united.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Secularism holds that political authority comes from the people and not from a religion, and that the state recognises no religion's claims; the 1905 French law rests on the sovereignty of the people.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Strict laïcité, the model in the 1905 law and its later applications, bars religious symbols for officials and in state schools, though the American separationist and accommodationist strands allow them, so adherents are split in degree.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Secularism is a church-state doctrine with no foreign-policy position; adherents differ.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Secularism concerns religion and state; its liberal-democratic literature favours equal citizenship, which inherited office contradicts, but it states no view on this.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on credit institutions; adherents differ.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Secularism is about religion and state and takes no position on international lending; adherents differ.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Secularism takes no stated view; adherents differ on ecofeminist claims.

reification.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on reification; adherents split.

online-participation.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on online political participation; adherents differ.

open-government-data.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on open government data; adherents differ.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Secularism opposes the state enforcing religious law, which includes religious restrictions on marriage, and it protects freedom of conscience.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Secularism concerns religion and state and has no stated position on wealth; adherents differ.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Holyoake writes that secular education is not atheistic and that atheism cannot be a secularist tenet, and Wikipedia sets state atheism apart from secularism because it denies freedom of belief.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: No stated position; adherents are split on charity versus state provision.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Who may lead a religious body is internal religious affairs, in which secularism, as laïcité and the NSS state it, has the state take no part.

god-not-male.rationale: How God is described is a doctrinal question, and secularism holds that the state takes no position on doctrine and does not intervene in it.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Judging scripture is religious interpretation, which laïcité and the NSS leave to believers: the state does not intervene in matters of doctrine.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Secularism concerns church and state, not national identity; adherents split between civic and linguistic views of the nation.

free-public-college.rationale: A policy question outside church and state; secularists are spread across the economic spectrum.

capital-controls.rationale: Economic policy is outside the doctrine and adherents differ.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Holyoake confines secularism to questions testable in this life and excludes questions of deity, and laïcité bars the state from positions on doctrine, so the unity of religions is outside the doctrine.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Secularism has no position on nuclear arms; adherents differ.

workers-own-party.rationale: A doctrine on church and state, with no stated view on labour parties; adherents differ.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: No stated view; French laicite stresses civic integration but secularism does not address language.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Secularism is compatible with procedural and substantive views of democracy; adherents are split.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Welfare design is outside secularism's concern; adherents are split.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Secularists criticise religious authority but the doctrine does not itself assert this claim; adherents are split.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Secularism has no position on gender-equality machinery; adherents are split.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Under laïcité the government refrains from taking positions on religious doctrine, and Holyoake excludes theological questions from secularism, so how scripture is read is left to believers.

national-church-status.rationale: Core secularism holds the state should recognise and privilege no religion; the 1905 French law states the Republic neither recognises nor subsidises any faith, and Wikipedia lists equal treatment of religions as a defining principle.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Strands differ: the French republican model rejects ethnic autonomy while liberal-pluralist secularists accept it; the doctrine itself is silent.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: A church-state doctrine with no stated view on borders; adherents are split.

simple-living.rationale: Secularism leaves personal ways of life to individual conscience and is neutral on asceticism versus abundance.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Keeping religion and politics separate is the core of secularism, and organising politics by denomination contradicts it.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Secularists split between natural-law and positivist views of law; the doctrine does not decide it.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Secularism is neutral on patriotism and economic politics; adherents range across the spectrum.

material-over-identity.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on left priorities; adherents differ.

missingStatements.text: State schools should not provide religious instruction.
missingStatements.rationale: Holyoake stressed secular instruction in schools and the 1905 French law banned religious instruction in state primary schools.

notes: Accommodationist secularists (India, pillarized states) would answer school-voucher, religious-symbol and personal-law questions differently from strict laïcité. Deepen pass (2026-10-29): searched Holyoake's English Secularism (full text), the 1905 law, laïcité, and the programmes of the NSS and Americans United for the economy, world, ecology, technology, means and globalism themes. Beyond church-state questions they state only opposition to public money for religious schools (vouchers) and the state's neutrality on doctrine; on assisted dying, abortion and same-sex marriage they ask only that religious doctrine not decide, and the NSS says its members differ. Several earlier medium answers deduced from general equality were lowered.
